main_text.head: Quæstio VI.

head.i: An mordacces, an vero edentulas expediat inter amicos esse facetias.

main_text.p: VOluptatis excessum refugiunt Sensus, & ingrati alicujus gestiunt consortio: Acria, amara, salsa, quæ pungunt ac vellicant inter epulas amat Gustatus; saccharo ac bellariis semper vesci, etiam fæminæ puerique abnuunt: Et habet perpetuum illud ac exundans inter amicos obsequium, quo pertæsum sæpe faciat, quem nimium delinit: huic si de jocis acre quid & salsum asperseris, amicum nauseâ prohibuisti: officia tua sic condita, palatum semper irritant, salivam semper movent. Ingenium etiam, quod sine exercitio

page.notes: The initial V is a decorated woodcut letter, transcribed as V. The word "VOluptatis" begins with that initial. Some words in the body are faint or show-through from the facing page (e.g. "vesci", "Et"); readings there are as printed but uncertain. The signature reads "I 3" as printed, with the 3 possibly a mis-set numeral.
